code.title: Note File Writer
code.description:
A simple journal app saves each note into a text file before showing it on screen. Read two lines of text and store them in the file note20.txt, one per line. Then reopen the file, read both lines back and print them.

Input Format:
Two lines of text; each line may contain spaces.

Output Format:
File contains:
<line 1>
<line 2>

Constraints:
Each line is 1 to 50 characters.
code.sampleinput2:
C++ streams rock
Files store data
code.input1:
Data line one
Data line two
code.output1:
File contains:
Data line one
Data line two
code.output3:
File contains:
x
y
code.sampleoutput1:
File contains:
Hello file
Second line
code.sampleoutput2:
File contains:
C++ streams rock
Files store data

code.title: Numbers File Sum Reader
code.description:
A mini calculator stores a list of numbers in a file and totals it by reading the file back. Read N and then N integers, write all of them into nums20.txt separated by spaces, then reopen the file and compute how many numbers are stored and their sum.

Input Format:
First line: N. Second line: N integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Count: <count read from file>
Sum: <sum read from file>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= each integer <= 1000
code.output3:
Count: 6
Sum: 1
code.sampleoutput1:
Count: 5
Sum: 150

code.title: Sentence Length from File
code.description:
A typing trainer stores a practice sentence in a file and reports its length by reading the file back. Read one sentence (a single line) and write it to sent20.txt. Then reopen the file, read the sentence back and print it together with its length.

Input Format:
One line of text (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Stored: <sentence read from file>
Length: <length of the stored sentence>

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 100
code.output2:
Stored: The quick brown fox jumps
Length: 25
code.output3:
Stored: Words with spaces inside
Length: 24
code.sampleoutput1:
Stored: Files hold text
Length: 15

code.title: Append Note Builder
code.description:
A sticky-notes tool keeps one note per line in app20.txt. The program always starts the file with the base line 'Notes started' and then appends the note typed by the user using append mode. Finally it prints every line of the finished file.

Input Format:
One line of text (the user note; may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Every line of app20.txt after the append, in order (the base line first, then the user note).

Constraints:
1 <= note length <= 60
code.output3:
Notes started
last note of the day
code.sampleoutput1:
Notes started
buy milk

code.title: Student Mark File Record
code.description:
A teacher assistant stores a mark in a file before printing it. Read a student name (single word) and a mark (integer), write 'name mark' into stud20.txt, then reopen the file, read the record back and print it in the required format.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: name (single word) and mark (integer).

Output Format:
Student: <name>
Mark: <mark>

Constraints:
0 <= mark <= 100
code.output3:
Student: Ravi
Mark: 59
code.sampleoutput1:
Student: Arjun
Mark: 92

code.title: Missing File Open Check
code.description:
A safe reader always checks whether a file opened successfully. First try to open missing20.txt for reading (it does not exist yet) and print whether it is open. Then read a message from input, create missing20.txt, store the message in it, reopen the file for reading and print the new open state plus the message.

Input Format:
One line of text (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
First open: <1 if open, else 0>
Second open: <1 if open, else 0>
File says: <message read back from the file>

Constraints:
1 <= message length <= 60
code.output1:
First open: 0
Second open: 1
File says: first run text
code.output2:
First open: 0
Second open: 1
File says: single
code.output3:
First open: 0
Second open: 1
File says: text with several words here
code.sampleoutput1:
First open: 0
Second open: 1
File says: recovered message
code.sampleoutput2:
First open: 0
Second open: 1
File says: error handled

code.title: Shop Receipt File Writer
code.description:
A shop counter writes each purchased item into bill20.txt before totalling the bill. Read N and then N item-price pairs (item is a single word, price an integer). Store each pair on its own line, then reopen the file, print every line and the total of all prices.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with an item (single word) and an integer price.

Output Format:
One line per item: <item> : <price>
Then: Total: <sum of prices>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10, 1 <= price <= 10000
code.output3:
alpha : 1
beta : 2
gamma : 3
Total: 6
code.sampleoutput1:
pen : 10
book : 45
bag : 500
Total: 555

code.title: Visitor Log Append Mode
code.description:
A gate keeps a visitor log in vis20.txt. The first two visitors of the day are written into a fresh file, and a late visitor is added using append mode. Print the complete log exactly as stored in the file.

Input Format:
One line with three visitor names (single words) separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Visit: <first>
Visit: <second>
Visit: <third>

Constraints:
Each name is 1 to 20 characters.

Visit: Vikas
Visit: Zoya

Visit: Aditi
Visit: Ravi
Visit: Sam

Visit: Neha
Visit: Om
Visit: Dev

code.title: Temperature Log Extremes
code.description:
A weather station stores every reading in temp20.txt and then reports the extremes by reading the file. Read N and then N integer readings, store each on its own line, then reopen the file and report how many readings were stored plus the maximum and the minimum.

Input Format:
First line: N. Second line: N integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Readings: <count read from file>
Max: <maximum reading>
Min: <minimum reading>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50, -100 <= each reading <= 100
code.output3:
Readings: 2
Max: 99
Min: -99
code.sampleoutput1:
Readings: 4
Max: 35
Min: 28

code.title: Config File Echo
code.description:
A settings loader keeps preferences in conf20.txt as key=value lines. Read N and then N key/value pairs, store each as key=value, then reopen the file, read it line by line, split every line at the '=' character and print the key and value.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with a key (single word) and a value (single word).

Output Format:
One line per setting: Key: <key> Value: <value>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 8; keys and values contain no '=' and no spaces.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 8; keys and values contain no '=' and no spaces
code.output2:
Key: a Value: 1
Key: b Value: 2
Key: c Value: 3
Key: d Value: 4
code.output3:
Key: key1 Value: value1
Key: key2 Value: value2
code.sampleoutput1:
Key: host Value: localhost
Key: port Value: 8080
Key: mode Value: debug
code.sampleoutput2:
Key: user Value: admin
Key: token Value: xyz123

code.title: Stock CSV Quantity Tally
code.description:
A small warehouse keeps its stock in stock20.csv using item,qty lines. Read N and then N item/quantity pairs (item is a single word, quantity an integer), store each as item,qty, then reopen the file, read it line by line, split each line at the comma manually and print the stock table plus the total quantity.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with an item (single word) and an integer quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line per record: <item> -> <qty>
Then: Total qty: <sum of all quantities>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10, 0 <= qty <= 500
code.output2:
a -> 1
b -> 2
c -> 3
d -> 4
Total qty: 10
code.output3:
x -> 0
y -> 0
z -> 7
Total qty: 7
code.sampleoutput1:
pen -> 12
book -> 5
bag -> 2
Total qty: 19

code.title: Append Versus Overwrite Demo
code.description:
A mode tester shows what out mode and append mode do to the same file. It first plants old content in mode20.txt, then reopens the file in plain out mode with the first input word (erasing what was there), appends the second word, and finally appends the third word. After every step the whole file is read back and printed, so the mode effects are visible.

Input Format:
One line with three words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
After overwrite: <file content after the out-mode write>
After append: <content after appending the second word>
Final content: <content after appending the third word>

Constraints:
Each word is 1 to 12 characters.
code.output1:
After overwrite: go
After append: gostop
Final content: gostopwait
code.output2:
After overwrite: a
After append: ab
Final content: abc
code.output3:
After overwrite: Hi
After append: Hibye
Final content: Hibyemaybe
code.sampleoutput1:
After overwrite: Sun
After append: SunMoon
Final content: SunMoonStar
code.sampleoutput2:
After overwrite: one
After append: onetwo
Final content: onetwothree

code.title: Failed Open Recovery Drill
code.description:
A recovery tool verifies a file is really missing before creating it. First attempt to open nope20.txt for reading and report the open state. Then read N lines from input, create nope20.txt with them, reopen the file, report the new state and print every stored line numbered.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines of text.

Output Format:
First attempt: <1 if open, else 0>
Reopened: <1 if open, else 0>
Then one line per stored line: <i>: <line>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 5, each line 1 to 40 characters
code.output1:
First attempt: 0
Reopened: 1
1: alpha
2: beta
3: gamma
code.output3:
First attempt: 0
Reopened: 1
1: x y
2: a b
code.sampleoutput1:
First attempt: 0
Reopened: 1
1: apple pie
2: code daily
code.sampleoutput2:
First attempt: 0
Reopened: 1
1: single line only

code.title: Word Count Per Line
code.description:
A reading coach counts the words of every sentence it stores. Read N and then N sentences, store them in lines20.txt, then reopen the file and read it line by line, printing how many words each line holds. Words are separated by one or more spaces.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines of text (sentences).

Output Format:
One line per sentence: Line <i>: <word count> words

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 5, 1 <= words per line <= 10
code.sampleinput1:
2
learn file handling
write and read
code.input1:
3
alpha beta
gamma
delta epsilon zeta
code.input3:
2
one two three four
five six
code.output1:
Line 1: 2 words
Line 2: 1 words
Line 3: 3 words
code.output3:
Line 1: 4 words
Line 2: 2 words
code.sampleoutput1:
Line 1: 3 words
Line 2: 3 words

code.title: File Copy via getline
code.description:
A backup helper copies one text file to another. Read N and then N lines into src20.txt, then copy the whole content line by line into dst20.txt using a getline loop, and finally print the contents of the copy.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines of text.

Output Format:
The lines of dst20.txt in order.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 5, each line 1 to 40 characters
code.sampleinput1:
2
copy me please
line number two
code.input3:
2
mix of words and numbers
final backup row
code.output3:
mix of words and numbers
final backup row
code.sampleoutput1:
copy me please
line number two

code.title: Word Tally from File
code.description:
A word-game scorer stores a sentence in tally20.txt and then counts words by reading tokens from the file. Read the sentence and a query word, store the sentence, reopen the file and count the total number of tokens and how many of them equal the query word.

Input Format:
Line 1: a sentence (may contain spaces). Line 2: the query word (single word).

Output Format:
Total words: <token count>
<query> count: <matches>

Constraints:
The sentence has 1 to 20 words; the query word is a single word with no spaces
code.inputconstrains: The sentence has 1 to 20 words; the query word is a single word

the cat saw the dog and the cat ran
cat
code.sampleinput2:
files store words in plain text
words
code.input3:
code every day code all night
code
code.output3:
Total words: 6
code count: 2
code.sampleoutput1:
Total words: 9
cat count: 2

code.title: Bank Ledger Statement Builder
code.description:
A mini banking app records every transaction in ledger20.txt with the running balance. Read N and then N transactions (a character D for deposit or W for withdrawal, followed by an integer amount). The balance starts at 0. For each transaction write a line 'type amount Balance: <new balance>' to the file. Then reopen the file, read it line by line, parse every line to recover the amount and the running balance, print the full statement, and finally report the final balance and the largest single transaction amount, both computed from the file.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with a character (D or W) and an integer amount.

Output Format:
One statement line per transaction exactly as stored.
Then: Final balance: <balance parsed from the last line>
Largest transaction: <largest amount parsed from the file>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, 1 <= amount <= 10000; the balance may go negative
code.output1:
D 42 Balance: 42
Final balance: 42
Largest transaction: 42
code.output2:
W 50 Balance: -50
D 20 Balance: -30
W 30 Balance: -60
Final balance: -60
Largest transaction: 50
code.output3:
D 10000 Balance: 10000
W 10000 Balance: 0
Final balance: 0
Largest transaction: 10000
code.sampleoutput1:
D 500 Balance: 500
W 200 Balance: 300
D 300 Balance: 600
W 100 Balance: 500
Final balance: 500
Largest transaction: 500
code.sampleoutput2:
D 1000 Balance: 1000
D 250 Balance: 1250
W 750 Balance: 500
Final balance: 500
Largest transaction: 1000

code.title: Two File Merge Reader
code.description:
A statistics tool stores even numbers and odd numbers in two separate files and then merges them. Read E and then E sorted even integers (store them in even20.txt, one per line), then O and then O sorted odd integers (store them in odd20.txt, one per line). Reopen both files and merge-read them like a merge sort: always print the smaller unread value first, then continue until both files are exhausted.

Input Format:
Line 1: E. Line 2: E sorted even integers. Line 3: O. Line 4: O sorted odd integers.

Output Format:
The merged ascending sequence, one number per line.

Constraints:
1 <= E, O <= 20; numbers within each file are sorted ascending; 0 <= value <= 1000
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= E, O <= 20; each file sorted ascending; 0 <= value <= 1000

code.title: Student Registry Query from File
code.description:
A registrar stores student records in reg20.txt as 'name mark' lines and then answers lookups by re-reading the file. Read N records and store them. Then read Q and Q query names; for every query reopen the file, scan the stored records and print the mark or 'Not found'.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with a name (single word) and an integer mark. Then a line with Q. Then Q lines, each with one query name.

Output Format:
First: Records stored: <N>
Then one line per query: <query>: <mark> or <query>: Not found

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10, 0 <= mark <= 100, 0 <= Q <= 5; query names may repeat or miss
code.output3:
Records stored: 2
x: 10
y: 20
z: Not found
code.whitelist: ifstream, ofstream, cin, cout, string, bool
code.sampleoutput1:
Records stored: 3
Meera: 78
Om: Not found

code.title: Audit Trail Session Logger
code.description:
A security tool writes one audit file across three sessions. For session 1 it opens audit20.txt in plain out mode (fresh start); sessions 2 and 3 open the same file in append mode. Each session writes the header 'Session k' followed by k entry words, one per line. Read the three sessions from input, write them, then reopen the file and print the complete audit trail with line numbers and the total line count.

Input Format:
One line with three session descriptions: k1 entry... k2 entry... k3 entry... (each session starts with its entry count followed by that many single-word entries).

Output Format:
One numbered line per file line: <i>: <line>
Then: Total lines: <count>

Constraints:
0 <= entries per session <= 3; each entry is a single word of 1 to 12 characters
